stem: An online marketplace wants an alarm that automatically scales its checkout fleet when latency rises, and separately wants to see exactly which downstream call is slowing a specific checkout request. Which TWO services address these two needs? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch alarm on a latency metric to trigger Auto Scaling
Configure a Route 53 health check on the checkout endpoint to detect when it stops responding
Search aggregated application logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights for the affected time window
Add a custom CloudWatch dashboard widget that graphs per-service latency
Enable AWS X-Ray tracing to build a service map and trace the slow downstream call

rationale: A CloudWatch alarm on a latency metric is exactly the mechanism that watches a threshold and can trigger Auto Scaling actions when latency rises, addressing the scaling need. AWS X-Ray traces an individual request across the downstream services it calls and builds a service map that pinpoints which specific call added the latency, addressing the tracing need. A Route 53 health check monitors whether an endpoint is reachable so DNS can fail over to a secondary site; it reports up-or-down status, not a latency metric, so it does not trigger scaling the way an alarm does. Searching aggregated logs with CloudWatch Logs Insights can surface patterns across many log entries for a time window, but it does not trace a single request's path through multiple services, so it cannot point to the one downstream call that slowed one specific request. A custom CloudWatch dashboard widget only visualizes metrics that are already being collected per service; like Logs Insights, it shows aggregated numbers rather than tracing an individual request across service boundaries.
